description: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC %) of five different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, and IKE—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is plotted on a logarithmic x-axis ranging from 10⁰ to 10³. The y-axis represents accuracy in percentage points, ranging from 40% to 65%. The Base method is shown as a black line with circle markers, starting at approximately 39% accuracy and rising slightly to about 44% by the end of the range. The MEND method is represented by a brown line with diamond markers, beginning near 45% and increasing steadily to around 57%. The FT method is a blue line with triangle markers, starting at about 40% and rising to approximately 47%. The MEMIT method is a purple line with star markers, beginning near 44% and increasing to about 55%. The IKE method is a red line with triangle markers, starting at roughly 43% and rising to approximately 50%. The green line with square markers, which appears to represent a combined or averaged performance metric, starts at about 51% and increases to nearly 66%.
